official.deadline_note: 19 February 2026, 11 pm CET (closure of the online system) for semester/partial, full degree and study visit applications; summer courses closed 27 February 2026, 5 pm CET. National scholarship offices of bilateral partners apply their own internal deadlines for nominated applicants. This 2026/2027 call is the latest published by Tempus Public Foundation; the programme runs an annual cycle and the 2027/2028 successor call had not been published at the date of verification.
official.application_cycle: 2026/2027 academic year (call decided by the Board of Trustees of Tempus Public Foundation on 27 November 2025)
official.status_note: Tempus Public Foundation's applicant page currently publishes the 2026/2027 call (Board decision 27 November 2025); its central deadline of 19 February 2026 has passed. The programme is an annual cycle - new bilateral calls are announced on the same official page - so applicants should wait for the 2027/2028 call document and its dates.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'The tuition fee is covered by the Hungarian state.' (Scholarship Allowances section, applicable to both partial/semester and full degree studies calls)
benefits: Bachelor and Master partial/semester and full degree studies: 56 600 HUF/month (explicitly 'not covering the cost of living')
Doctoral partial/semester studies: 140 000 HUF/month in the 1st and 2nd year; 180 000 HUF/month in the 3rd and 4th year ('not necessarily covering the cost of living')

Study visits - postgraduate applicants: 80 000 HUF/month stipend plus 70 000 HUF/month accommodation allowance; postdoctoral applicants: 120 000 HUF/month stipend plus 80 000 HUF/month accommodation allowance
Tuition fee covered by the Hungarian state
Summer courses: the scholarship is the participation fee, which includes the classes, accommodation and meals
Stipend source: Hungarian State budget; scholarship-holders nominated from the Czech Republic, Poland and the Slovak Republic receive their stipend from their sending relation
eligibility: Partial/semester bachelor or master studies: students enrolled outside Hungary at bachelor or master level (incl. one-tier master) with at least one completed semester, primarily those majoring in Hungarian language and literature
Partial/semester doctoral studies: applicants enrolled in a PhD programme at an accredited higher education institution in a foreign country

Full degree studies: foreign citizens with a secondary school graduation or higher education degree in any field of studies or arts; doctoral applicants must hold a master's degree and pass the entrance exam at the receiving institution
Applicants must be 18 years old by 01 September 2026; there is no upper age limit

Not entitled to apply: holders of Hungarian immigration/settlement permits or permanent residents of Hungary, foreign citizens employed under the Hungarian Labour Law, foreign citizens residing in Hungary, those already started the studies they apply for in Hungary, and those who failed to submit the final report for previous Bilateral State Scholarships
Applicants may not hold another Hungarian state or EU-financed scholarship for the same purpose and time period
requirements: Submit a complete application into the Tempus Public Foundation online system (scholarship.hu) before the deadline; applications by post or e-mail are not accepted
Country-nominated applicants must also submit an application to the responsible scholarship office of the sending country, which works with its own deadlines
At most one application per scholarship type; where several are submitted, the last one is considered valid

Full degree applicants must also submit the admission application directly to the selected Hungarian higher education institution; participation in the admission process is the responsibility of the applicant
Scholarship-holders must stay in Hungary for the entire period of their studies (excluding school and public holidays) and submit an online mobility report within 30 days after finishing the stay
documents: Tempus Public Foundation application form, signed and dated by hand, scanned and uploaded
Certificate of enrolment issued by the home institution, including the expected date of graduation
Copy of valid passport or identity card
Motivation letter of minimum 1 and maximum 2 pages, according to the published template
Copy of Transcript of Records (for master studies also a copy of the bachelor's degree)
Proof of language proficiency required for the completion of the studies (at least B2 knowledge)

Preliminary Acceptance Letter issued by the head of department and the international office of a Hungarian higher education institution, dated, stamped and signed on institutional letterhead with contact details

Doctoral partial studies additionally: detailed work plan of 2-5 pages, copy of the highest degree/diploma, and two letters of recommendation from recognized experts (max 6 months old, signers different from the acceptance letter)
Art scholarships additionally: link to the webpage of 5 works of art (fine/applied artists) or 3 performances of different styles (performing artists)
selection_criteria: Formal eligibility check by the Hungarian side, then professional scoring by Tempus Public Foundation's external experts (maximum 57 points for bachelor/master, 65 points for doctoral applicants)

Scoring: background of the applicant and relevance of the scholarship (10), quality of motivation letter/work plan (20), language knowledge (7), evaluation of letters of recommendation for doctoral applicants (8), overall impression on the application (5)
Additional points for studies held in Hungarian language (10), new applicants (5), and nominees of the foreign partner (up to 30)
Preference is given to applicants nominated by their sending relation, those applying for studies held in Hungarian and new applicants; ties are ranked by the nomination letter/work plan
Decisions are made by the Board of Trustees of Tempus Public Foundation; there is no appeal against the decision (objection may be lodged within 30 days of notification)
Any undue influence on the professional evaluation causes immediate exclusion
coverage: Tuition fee - covered by the Hungarian state
Monthly stipend paid by the receiving higher education institution (partial/semester and full degree studies) or by Tempus Public Foundation
Accommodation allowance for study-visit applicants (70 000/80 000 HUF per month depending on level)
Summer course participation fee including classes, accommodation and meals
Not covered: travel expenses to Hungary, within Hungary and back to the country of origin; visa fees; accommodation in a student dormitory (paid by the scholarship-holder); accompanying persons
application_method: Register with a user ID and password in the online system at scholarship.hu
Fill in the CV tab and upload the documents listed in the call under 'Documents to be submitted'
Submit the complete application before the deadline (19 February 2026, 11 pm CET for the 2026/2027 cycle)
Country-nominated applicants: in addition, submit the application and documents to the national scholarship office of the sending country as early as possible
Full degree applicants: separately contact the Hungarian host institution and take part in its admission/entrance exam process
TPF may return an application once for correction during the formal check; uncorrected applications may be rejected without assessment
official.application_route: Apply online via scholarship.hu (also through the home country's national scholarship office for nominated applicants); receive the decision by e-mail.
official.citizenship_residency: Partial/full degree individual applications: citizens of Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Japan (Hungarian language and culture only), Korean Republic (Hungarian language and culture only), Latvia, Lithuania, Luxemburg, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, San Marino, Spain, Switzerland, Sweden, Slovakia, Slovenia, UK and USA may apply directly. Nominated applications may be submitted by citizens of Bulgaria, People's Republic of China (exclusively in Hungarian language and culture), Croatia, Czech Republic, Poland, Romania, Slovakia and Slovenia. Applicants holding a Hungarian settlement permit, permanent residence in Hungary or employed under Hungarian labour law are excluded.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is exclusively for foreign applicants from partner or individually-eligible countries; Hungarian residency, settlement permits and Hungarian employment exclude applicants.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Studies in any field of arts or sciences at any accredited Hungarian higher education institution; applicants from China, Japan and the Republic of Korea are restricted to Hungarian language and culture studies.
official.research_requirement: Doctoral partial studies require a precise and detailed work plan of 2-5 pages (novelty/justification of the topic, methodology, schedule and subtasks are scored) plus two letters of recommendation from recognized experts in the relevant discipline.
official.duration: Semester/partial studies: 3-10 months (one or two semesters); full degree studies: bachelor 36 / master 24 / doctoral 36 / one-tier master 48 months; short or long-term study visits: 3 days - 6 months; summer courses: 2-4 weeks. Partial studies implementation period: 1 September 2026 - 31 July 2027, not postponable to the following academic year.
official.description: Hungarian bilateral state scholarships are based on scientific and educational cooperation agreements between the governments of two countries, offering foreign higher education students, researchers and lecturers places at accredited Hungarian higher education institutions for semester/partial or full degree studies, study visits or summer courses. Tempus Public Foundation, the Hungarian national scholarship office, runs the call with tuition covered by the Hungarian state and a monthly stipend from the state budget.
official.english_requirement: At least B2 knowledge in the language of instruction, proven by a language exam certificate or a certificate issued by the sending institution, foreign Hungarian Cultural Institute, lectorate or consul, written in Hungarian or English; applicants for Hungarian-language partial studies (except Hungarian majors studying in Hungarian) need no minimum Hungarian level, and summer courses accept any kind of certificate of at least B2-level English knowledge. There is no published IELTS/TOEFL requirement.

not_confirmed: 2027/2028 call dates and deadline (not yet published on the official pages at verification date)
Whether the stipend amounts remain unchanged in the next cycle, as the call is conditional on Tempus Public Foundation receiving the necessary state funds
verification.notes: Amounts, deadlines, coverage and documents taken from the Tempus Public Foundation 2026/2027 call PDFs (partial studies, full degree, study visits, summer courses) and its bilateral scholarship applicant page on en.tka.hu.

applicant_utility.summary: This scholarship pays tuition in Hungary plus a fixed monthly stipend - 56 600 HUF for bachelor/master students and 140 000-180 000 HUF for doctoral students - but the call states plainly that this does not cover living costs, so treat it as tuition relief plus partial living support, not full funding. If you are from one of the 30-odd individual-application countries you can apply directly through scholarship.hu, but if your country is a nominated partner (e.g. Bulgaria, Croatia, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Czech Republic, China) you must go through your national scholarship office first and meet its earlier internal deadline. The one make-or-break document is the dated, stamped Preliminary Acceptance Letter from your Hungarian host institution's head of department and international office - secure it in January at the latest for a mid-February deadline. Master's applicants must already be enrolled abroad with at least one completed semester; doctoral applicants get scored on a 2-5 page work plan and two recommendation letters.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Currently enrolled master's students or PhD candidates from eligible European/North American/Asian countries who have a concrete research or study plan and can secure a preliminary acceptance letter from a Hungarian host institution before mid-February.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears in the individual-application list in the call PDF, or identify your national scholarship office and its internal deadline (usually well before February)
Email prospective Hungarian departments/international offices early to obtain the dated, stamped and signed Preliminary Acceptance Letter on institutional letterhead
Prepare a B2-level language certificate in the language of instruction (or evidence of Hungarian for Hungarian-taught programmes), issued by your institution or a Hungarian cultural institute
Write the motivation letter strictly to the 1-2 page template and, for doctoral applicants, the 2-5 page work plan
Register at scholarship.hu early, since only complete applications submitted before the 11 pm CET deadline count and formal-check corrections are allowed only once
Verify you hold no other Hungarian state or EU scholarship for the same period and that any previous Bilateral State Scholarship final report was submitted
common_rejection_risks: No preliminary acceptance letter from a Hungarian institution, or one missing signatures, stamp, date or contact details
Documents in languages other than Hungarian, English, French or German without official translations
Language proof below B2 or issued without institutional letterhead (Hungarian as a major still requires Hungarian-taught studies)
Applying after the national office's internal deadline instead of Tempus's February deadline
Submitting a plan that overlaps other Hungarian-state funding for the same period, or being disqualified for non-residence rules (residing or being employed in Hungary)
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel to and within Hungary, visa and residence permit fees, dormitory accommodation, health insurance gaps for non-EU students before the TAJ card is issued, and most general living expenses - the stipend explicitly does not cover the cost of living, and accommodation is paid by the scholarship-holder.
document_audit: Recommendation letters must be no older than 6 months and cannot be signed by the same person who signed the acceptance letter
The acceptance letter must carry the head of department AND the international office, dated, stamped, with contact details
Master's applicants need the bachelor's degree copy plus the last completed semester transcript; bachelor applicants only the last semester transcript
The hand-signed application form must be scanned and uploaded while retaining the original
Certificate of enrolment must state the expected graduation date
Art applicants must supply online portfolio links (5 works or 3 performances), with creation dates
alerts: The 2026/2027 central deadline was 19 February 2026 (summer courses 27 February 2026); the scholarship runs annually, so watch for the next call, published on the same page and re-check the stipend figures in that document
Czech, Polish and Slovak nominees are paid by their own sending office, so the amount in this call does not apply to them
The scholarship cannot be postponed to a later academic year and the stay must start within 1 September 2026 - 31 July 2027
Failing the online mobility report within 30 days after the stay excludes you from all future Bilateral State Scholarships
Technical assistance stops at 4 pm CET on deadline day and the system closes at 11 pm CET
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply via scholarship.hu (plus your national office if nominated), formal eligibility check, external expert scoring (max 57/65 points incl. up to 30 for partner nomination), Board of Trustees decision notified by e-mail; for full degrees you must separately pass the Hungarian institution's entrance exam.
